programme.title: The Peloponnesian War

programme.title: The Peloponnesian War

programme.title: The Peloponnesian War

programme.title: Famous Greeks
programme.desc: A conflict before the walls of Troy; as Greek commander-in-chief, Agamemnon is in over his head; excelling in the virtues he lacks is Achilles; Homer's genius transforms their power struggle into a timeless lesson in the moral dimension of politics.

programme.title: Famous Greeks
programme.desc: Homer turns the Trojan prince Hector, the Greeks' chief foe, into the noblest hero of "The Iliad"; a patriot, soldier, devoted husband and father, Hector embodies the virtues most admired by the Greeks and their tragic vision of life.

programme.title: Masterpieces of Ancient Greek Literature

programme.title: Masterpieces of Ancient Greek Literature

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Examining the features of late medieval culture in Italy that pave the way for the Renaissance; in painting, Giotto di Bondone evolves a proto-Renaissance style in contrast to the prevailing late-Gothic style.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Around 1400, a European-wide style known as International Gothic flourishes in Italy; artists including Lorenzo Monaco and Gentile da Fabriano retain the style; others, such as Lorenzo Ghiberti, develop a new style that is known as Renaissance.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Architecture is central to understanding the birth of the Renaissance; it is in Florence that the first great buildings of the Renaissance are constructed; looking at the buildings of Filippo Brunelleschi and the bronze doors of Lorenzo Ghiberti.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Donatello is a key Italian artist of the 15th century; tracing Donatello's work until he moves to Padua in 1443; Luca della Robbia's choir gallery for the Florence Cathedral is in direct competition with Donatello's choir gallery for the same church.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: The first of two lectures on Masaccio examines his "Pisa Altarpiece"; studying Masaccio's monumental fresco "The Trinity", with attention to his introduction of one-point perspective.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Studying Masaccio's principal frescoes for the Brancacci Chapel, with special attention to their melding of style and narrative content; Masaccio undertakes the project with Masolino.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.sub-title: Fra Angelico and Fra Filippo Lippi
programme.desc: Fra Angelico and Fra Filippo Lippi are leading painters in Florence after Masaccio's death; Fra Angelico switches between a late medieval style and a more realistic Renaissance manner; Fra Filippo Lippi's paintings combine charm and inward quietness.

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Paintings by three contrasting artists in Florence; Paolo Uccello is devoted to foreshortening; Andrea del Castagno finds ways to make figures look like painted sculptures; Domenico Veneziano introduces a tonal delicacy and pastel palette.
